lekker: good/nice/great — used to express approval or enjoyment
eish: expression of surprise, frustration, or dismay — often signals negative sentiment
ag shame: expression of sympathy or mild disappointment — context-dependent, often negative
ag: mild exclamation of frustration or dismissal — softens a complaint
howzit: greeting — hello/how are you — signals neutral or positive opening
ja nee: yes-no — expresses mixed feelings, resignation, or reluctant agreement — signals negative/neutral
braai: barbecue — social reference, usually neutral/positive context
robot: traffic light — common SA term, not related to automation
now now: soon but not immediately — implies mild urgency without panic
just now: at some point in the near future — vague timing, can imply frustration if response is awaited
china: friend/mate — informal address (not the country), neutral
hectic: intense/difficult/a lot — often indicates negative experience when describing a product issue
dagga: cannabis — substance reference, neutral in legal SA context
gogga: insect/bug — can be used metaphorically for software bugs in informal SA tech speak
jislaaik: exclamation of surprise or shock — negative sentiment signal
lank: very/a lot — intensifier, amplifies whatever follows (lank bad = very bad)
moer: hit/destroy — used colloquially as 'broken badly', strong negative
nè: isn't it/right — sentence-ending confirmation particle, neutral
voetsek: go away — very strong negative, explicit rejection
wena: you — Nguni pronoun, often used in mixed-language sentences
yoh: exclamation of surprise or concern — negative/alarmed signal
aikona: no/not at all — strong negation, negative signal
haibo: exclamation of disbelief or shock — negative sentiment
sawubona: hello/I see you — Zulu greeting, positive opening
sikhona: we are here/we are well — Zulu response to greeting, positive
hoe gaan dit: how is it going — Afrikaans greeting, neutral/positive
baie dankie: thank you very much — Afrikaans, positive/grateful
geen probleem: no problem — Afrikaans, positive resolution signal
dis nie reg nie: this is not right — Afrikaans complaint signal, negative
